draft.title: Showing character
card: The writer tells the reader what a character is like. For example: "Tariq was a generous boy."
The writer shows the character and lets the reader work it out. This can be done through what the character does, says or thinks, and how other characters react to them.
Example: Tariq hands his last biscuit to a hungry classmate. The reader sees he is generous without being told.
Another example: other students go quiet when Priya walks in. Their reaction suggests she is feared or respected.
draft.remember: Telling states what a character is like. Showing lets the reader work it out from clues.

a.q: Which sentence shows a character's nature indirectly?
opts: Lena stayed back to help the cleaner stack every chair
Lena was a kind and thoughtful girl
Lena had a very caring nature
Lena was known as a helpful person
a.why: The first option shows Lena's actions and lets the reader decide she is kind. The other three tell the reader what she is like, so they are direct.
a.clue: Which one gives an action instead of a label?

b.q: In a story, Jack's classmates move their bags off the seat beside him, then look away when he walks past. What does this show about Jack?
opts: Other characters' reactions hint that he is disliked
The writer states directly that Jack is unpopular
Jack's own thoughts reveal that he is lonely
Jack's dialogue shows that he is rude to others
b.why: The writer gives no label for Jack. The reader works out from how others react that he may be disliked. The other options name a direct statement, thoughts or dialogue, and none of these appear in the scene.
b.clue: Look at who is doing something in the scene, and what the writer does not say.

a.best: Lena stayed back to help the cleaner stack every chair

b.best: Other characters' reactions hint that he is disliked

problems.detail: Why (a) calls the right answer 'the first option', but the options are shown in random order. Here it is the third. The why should name the option by its content, not its position.

a.q: Which sentence reveals Lena's character indirectly?
opts: Lena stayed back after class to help stack the chairs
Lena was the kindest and most helpful girl in her class
Lena was a caring girl who put other people first
Lena was kind, patient and thoughtful with everyone
a.why: Staying back to stack the chairs is an action, so the reader works out for themselves that Lena is helpful. The sentences calling her kind, caring or thoughtful tell the reader what she is like, so they are direct, even though they add detail.
a.clue: Which one gives an action instead of a description?
